problems.stem: Which design move best supports multiple means of representation?
options: Providing content only as narrated audio
Offering captions, visual summaries, and readable text alternatives alongside the core media
Requiring every learner to use the exact same medium
Removing diagrams so only text remains
problems.explanation: UDL's representation principle encourages flexible access through multiple ways of perceiving the content.

problems.stem: What is the strongest example of multiple means of action and expression?
options: Allowing only a written essay because it is easiest to grade
Letting learners demonstrate understanding through an essay, podcast, presentation, or structured visual artifact
Using the same timed quiz for every objective
Replacing all assessments with attendance checks
problems.explanation: This principle is about flexible ways for learners to act, express, and demonstrate what they know.

problems.stem: Why does UDL emphasize multiple means of engagement?
options: Because every learner is motivated by the same competitive activity
Because motivation and emotional regulation differ across learners and contexts
Because accessibility is only about color contrast
Because engagement matters only after assessment is complete
problems.explanation: UDL recognizes that learners vary in how they engage, persist, and regulate their attention and motivation.

problems.stem: Why is WCAG-style contrast and keyboard support relevant to instructional design rather than just front-end engineering?
options: Because accessibility has no impact on whether learning is possible
Because inaccessible delivery creates artificial barriers that block learners from participating at all
Because semantic HTML matters only to search engines
problems.explanation: If learners cannot perceive or operate the environment, the instruction fails before any pedagogy can help.
